title: San Francisco hospitals: charity discounts against gross revenue, fiscal 2015-16 to 2024-25
question: Did San Francisco hospitals' charity care move with their revenue over the decade?
finding: Checked; nothing that bears on a case. San Francisco hospitals together wrote off 0.74% of gross patient revenue as charity in 2015-16 and 1.51% in 2024-25 ($555.5 million); together they reported a net loss of $203.7 million in 2024-25. No hospital is named in an open case; the files add two baseline years to the hospital series.
how: HCAI hospital annual financial disclosure complete data sets: fiscal 2015-16 and 2016-17 from the supplied workbooks, 2017-18 to 2024-25 from the Bay Area extracts already on disk; page 8 lines 350 and 355 (charity discounts) over line 30 (gross patient revenue). San Francisco = facility city.
limits: Gross charges are list prices, far above what is paid, so the share is small by construction. Charity care is only part of community benefit (Medi-Cal shortfalls, research and teaching are reported elsewhere). Hospital systems report some campuses together. Kaiser and public hospitals report on different bases.
